subject: CloudFabric: multi-year prepay — billing split & discount exception
messages:
From: Rachel Lee <rachel@cloudfabric.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-year prepay structure request

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so we can get the commercial review started. High-level: CloudFabric is looking at a 3-year, annualized prepay for Redwood inference capacity. Target commitment: roughly $450k/year list for year 1 (expected growth years 2–3).

We are evaluating two structures and would like Redwood's recommendation and list of what requires approval:
- Option A: 2yr prepay, billed annually, flat (no escalator) — target ~18% off list
- Option B: 3yr prepay, billed annually, with a 5% usage ramp credit applied in year 1 — target ~22% off list

Can you confirm: approvals needed for discounts >20%, whether Redwood will accept a split-year invoice schedule (e.g., PO for year 1, invoice upfront for 3-year), and any required language for SOW/MA? Procurement also asked for a sample invoice schedule and a template PO line.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement cycle is on a two-week sprint.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Lee
Head of Procurement, CloudFabric
Attachments: none
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel@cloudfabric.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay structure request

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clarity. Quick answers up front:
- Standard commercial: up to 20% discount on multi-year prepay can be approved by Sales + RevOps. Anything >20% needs Finance VP sign-off.
- We can support annualized prepay billed upfront per year; we also support a single upfront invoice for multiple years if desired (we prefer full upfront for accounting clarity).
- We can build a PO-friendly invoice schedule and a simple SOW addendum for ramp credits.

I'll put together a two-option commercial worksheet and route for approval. Laura — looping you for margin and to attach a pricing matrix.

Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel@cloudfabric.io>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom@cloudfabric.io>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed worksheet and invoice options (pricing_matrix.xlsx attached)

Hi Rachel / Tom,

Attached is an initial pricing matrix with two scenarios. Summary (rounded):
- 2-year annual prepay: $850k total, 18% discount (invoices: Year1 upfront, Year2 invoiced at renewal)
- 3-year annual prepay with ramp credit: $1.25M total, 22% discount (invoices: Years 1–3 upfront annually)

Notes / asks:
- The 22% level triggers a commercial exception. I will need Neha (Finance) to weigh in on whether we can approve up to 22% or whether we should cap at 20%.
- For CloudFabric's accounting, if you prefer a single upfront invoice for the full term, we can accommodate — just confirm PO routing and tax details.

Action items:
- Rachel: confirm whether CloudFabric prefers single upfront invoice or annual upfront invoicing.
- Tom: please share the PO template if procurement needs specific line items.

Attachments: pricing_matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed worksheet and invoice options (requires approval for >20%)

Markus / Laura — reviewing. Finance position: our standard approval threshold for multi-year prepay discounts is 20%. Exceptions up to 22% may be approved by Finance but require a deal memo that includes:
- Expected ARR and gross margin impact by year
- Confirmed payment schedule (CA cashflow)
- Any refunds/credits language for under-usage (we prefer usage true-ups not refunds)

If you want to pursue 22% for the 3yr option, I need the attached MA redline (CloudFabric_MA.pdf) populated with the payment terms and the margin math. If margin erosion is >8% absolute vs list, this escalates to the VP of Finance.

For now I can provisionally approve 21% provided we lock the invoice to annual upfront and remove refunds (instead, offer a year-1 ramp credit as a percentage applied to year 2).

Neha Kapoor
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
Attachments: CloudFabric_MA.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel@cloudfabric.io>, Tom Barnes <tom@cloudfabric.io>, CloudFabric Procurement <procurement@cloudfabric.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial proposal: CloudFabric 3yr annualized prepay (22% exception request)

Hi Rachel / Tom — following our internal review, attached is the commercial proposal and invoice schedule. Key points: 
- Option selected: 3-year annual prepay, $1.25M total list with a 22% committed discount, applied to each annual invoice.
- Ramp credit: 5% applied to year 1 consumption as an internal credit toward year 2 usage (no cash refunds).
- Invoice schedule: Redwood issues an invoice each year, due net 30; CloudFabric can elect to issue a single PO for the three-year commitment.
- Exception request: As Neha notes, 22% exceeds our standard 20% threshold. Neha has provisionally approved 21%; we are requesting Finance VP sign-off for the additional 1% to reach 22% to close the deal this quarter.

Attachments: pricing_matrix.xlsx
Related: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABC-CloudFabric-3241

Rachel — if procurement confirms single PO for the term and the PO line references the DocuSign envelope above, we'll prepare the final MA addendum and route to Legal. Can you please confirm preference on single PO vs annual POs?

Thanks,
Markus
From: Rachel Lee <rachel@cloudfabric.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom@cloudfabric.io>, CloudFabric Procurement <procurement@cloudfabric.io>
Date: 2026-03-25T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal: CloudFabric 3yr annualized prepay (22% exception request)

Markus — thanks. Procurement will route a single PO that references the DocuSign envelope and the line items in pricing_matrix.xlsx. We prefer a single PO for the full term — please confirm final invoice recipient and tax info so finance can process quickly.

Tom and I will review the MA redline and aim to return signed DocuSign within 3 business days once the VP of Finance sign-off is confirmed on the discount exception.

Best,
Rachel
